section: Red flags: 2024 cancellation of Ulises Toirac's show
problems: comedian's claims stated as fact: that authorities cancelled the show and that the culprits are at the theatre
dispute about other venues: Club Biky and Bertolt Brecht Theater Café points
before: Points stating as fact that Cuban authorities cancelled the show, the 'culprits' quote, the cancellation question, an Unverified line on his ideas, and a point on his May 2024 suspension at Club Biky and April ban at the Bertolt Brecht café.
after: Three Unverified points credited to Toirac on Facebook via CubaHeadlines (Olivia Torres, 20 June 2024): that authorities cancelled the Ateneo Hall show, that the people responsible are in the Ateneo Hall of the Terry Theater, and that he was denied work for his views. Club Biky and Bertolt Brecht points cut. Source marked (partisan).
reason: The page names the theatre ('the Ateneo Hall of the Terry Theater') and supports every quotation word for word, but the only account is Toirac's own post carried by an outlet openly opposed to the Cuban government, so each claim is Unverified and credited to him. The other venues are not this space. CubaNet and Diario de Cuba copies refused reads (researcher's log).

problems: not a dispute about the space: a theft with no dispute around it and a return of the object to the library
before: WIDER CONTEXT: theft of the Ortelius atlas between 1990 and 1993, sale to the Boston Athenaeum, identification in 1999 and return to the library on 6 April 2017 (OnCuba).
reason: OnCuba supports the facts, but a theft with nobody disputing it is not a finding under the research brief, and a return of a stolen object to the library is not a claim against it. File deleted.

problems: added descriptor: 'exiled writer Abel Sierra' (the page says he lives in the United States)
changed detail: 'two interviews and two reviews' (page: two interviews and reviews by two Cuban intellectuals)
before: texts by and about the exiled writer Abel Sierra disappeared from La Ventana ...: two interviews and two reviews of his essay Del otro lado del espejo ...
after: texts by and about the writer Abel Sierra, who lives in the United States, disappeared from La Ventana ...: two interviews, and reviews by two Cuban intellectuals of his essay Del otro lado del espejo ... SOURCES line marked as a Diario de Cuba and Connectas report carried by El Tiempo.
reason: El Tiempo (18 July 2021, Yoe Suárez, 'realizada para Diario de Cuba y Connectas') supports the removals, the Legna Rodríguez Iglesias search, the other names, the 'Eso es una excusa' reply and the 'ejercicio sistemático' quotation. Two descriptors were cut back to the page. It stays in WIDER CONTEXT because it predates November 2021.

section: Red flags: 2025 cancellation of a Pavel Giroud documentary screening
problems: repetition: the record's 14ymedio press item already states that organisers suspended the screening and that Giroud remarked ironically on it (Giroud's 'Apparently, they regretted' quotation cut)
cancellation stated in the outlet's voice; it is Giroud's report on Facebook
before: Three points: the festival cancelled the screening 'without any explanation (CiberCuba)'; Giroud's 'Apparently, they regretted scheduling my documentary' quotation; the Observatorio de Derechos Culturales statement.
after: Two points: Giroud said on Facebook that the 40th edition cancelled, without any explanation, the screening set for 1 February 2025 at the 23 and 12 cinema, which he described as 'part of the Jazz Festival program'; the Observatorio de Derechos Culturales statement. Source given by its full address and marked (partisan).
reason: The page ties the cinema screening to the festival in Giroud's own words ('part of the Jazz Festival program'), so the item stays. The cancellation is by the festival itself after November 2021, so it stays under Red flags. Editor: the 14ymedio press item already reports the suspension. This section adds the date, the venue and the Observatorio statement.

problems: repetition: the December 2020 police deployment and INSTAR's statement are already in the record's Hyperallergic 2020 press item
not the space: Bruguera taken to the Infanta police station (her detentions are already covered by the press item)
not read: Hyperallergic 7 October 2021 body behind a sign-up wall; the point concerns the founder, not INSTAR
before: Four points: The Art Newspaper on the 6 December 2020 police deployment and INSTAR's statement; Bruguera taken to the Infanta station; Hyperallergic on her 2021 departure deal; Unverified PEN joint statement on the 2023 film festival campaign.
after: One Unverified point from the PEN International joint statement of 7 December 2023 on the state campaign against INSTAR's fourth film festival (4 to 10 December 2023), with Bruguera's 2021 departure as the statement puts it. Only the PEN source is kept, marked (advocacy source).
reason: The Art Newspaper page supports its points but repeats what the record holds. The Hyperallergic body was not readable. The PEN statement supports each quoted phrase word for word. It is a joint statement by advocacy bodies, so the point stays Unverified. It sits in WIDER CONTEXT because the Cuban state neither funds nor controls INSTAR.

before: Three points on the 2006 US embargo ruling (NBC News, Mark Potter, 3 December 2006).
reason: Clean. NBC News supports the technical-help-only rule, the Bush administration's embargo ruling and its tourism reasoning, the restoration workers' reply, the Phillips quotation word for word and the planned licence reapplication. A US decision of 2006, made when the US neither funded nor controlled the museum, belongs in WIDER CONTEXT.
